name: Anganwadi Practices for Foundational Stage Education Scale (APFSES)
description: The National Education Policy 2020 repositioned the Anganwadi Centre (AWC) from a predominantly nutrition-delivery point to a formal site of foundational learning, extending the school stage downward to include children aged three to six years. This relocation of responsibility raises an empirical question that policy documents alone cannot answer: how adequately are Anganwadi Centres actually performing the educational practices now expected of them? The present study evaluates the classroom-level practices of Anganwadi Centres across five dimensions — infrastructure and learning environment, play-based pedagogical practices, curriculum and learning material use, assessment and record keeping, and parental and community engagement. A descriptive survey design was adopted, and data were collected from 80 Anganwadi workers selected through stratified random sampling from rural and urban projects. The Anganwadi Practices for Foundational Stage Education Scale (APFSES), a 40-item five-point Likert instrument developed and validated by the investigators (Cronbach's α = .91), was used for data collection. Data were analysed using SPSS version 25 through descriptive statistics, the independent samples t-test, Pearson product-moment correlation, and multiple linear regression.
